payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Its corrected, governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted after independent audit. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale, and an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that temperature.
VERDICT: REJECT - the audit measured 4,800 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, so describing 8,400 cycles as reaching that threshold is unsupported.

payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce electrolyte crossover. Its confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates. An independent audit retracted the original 12,000-cycle claim: it measured 4,800 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, while 8,400 is the corrected governing cycle-life figure.
